questions.q: Why is a silver-to-gold pipeline usually simpler than a bronze-to-silver one?
options: It reads data that's already clean by the time it runs — its job is aggregation, not cleaning
Silver-to-gold pipelines never actually need to run any transformations
Gold tables don't require any write operation at all
Silver-to-gold pipelines can't use the DataFrame API
questions.explain: Fewer transformation steps here is expected, not a sign something's missing.

questions.q: Why is mode("overwrite") often the right default for a gold table, unlike silver's MERGE?
options: Many gold tables are small enough to fully recompute each run — simpler than MERGE and just as correct
overwrite is always faster than MERGE regardless of table size
MERGE cannot be used on gold tables under any circumstances
Gold tables don't support the MERGE operation technically
questions.explain: The whole table gets rebuilt from all of silver each time, rather than merged incrementally.

questions.q: When would a gold table need incremental (MERGE-based) logic instead of overwrite?
options: For a genuinely large gold aggregate built from a silver table with billions of rows, where recomputing everything on every run gets too expensive
Every gold table always needs MERGE, without exception
Only when the gold table has fewer than 10 rows
Only if Unity Catalog governs the table
questions.explain: This is a real engineering tradeoff between overwrite's simplicity and MERGE's efficiency at scale.

questions.q: How does chaining bronze-to-silver and silver-to-gold into one job work?
options: Two tasks in one job, where the silver-to-gold task depends on the bronze-to-silver task finishing successfully first
They must always run as two completely separate, unrelated jobs
Gold automatically detects when silver has finished, with no explicit dependency
Task dependency isn't possible in Databricks Jobs
questions.explain: This reuses Lesson 11's task-chaining, guaranteeing gold never reads silver mid-update.

questions.q: What guarantee does chaining Task 1 and Task 2 in the correct order provide?
options: Task 2 (silver-to-gold) never reads silver mid-update, since it only starts after Task 1 (bronze-to-silver) finishes successfully
Both tasks always run at the exact same time, in parallel
Task 2 can run even if Task 1 fails
There's no real guarantee; task order is purely cosmetic
questions.explain: This is exactly the dependency mechanism Lesson 11 introduced for chaining tasks within one job.
